name: Kneebar from Carni
summary: The Kneebar is a straight leg lock that controls the hip and ankle while placing a fulcrum behind the knee, threatening knee extension when the attacker closes the hips.
description: Kneebar from Carni requires a separate hip and leg capture. Release the shoulder-lock configuration before setting a knee fulcrum and controlling the ankle.
overview:
The attacker has isolated one leg between the legs, with the opponent's knee aligned at the hip fulcrum and the ankle controlled. Carni is a shoulder-lock configuration. A kneebar needs a separately captured leg and a new hip-to-knee alignment; neither the Carni leg clamp nor its name supplies that alignment.

Confirm control of the opponent's thigh and ankle before considering a knee-extension attack. Use the legs to keep the opponent's hip from moving freely away. Place the knee at the hip fulcrum with the leg in a straight, non-twisted line. Hold the lower leg close without turning the foot into a rotational lock.

Drill the control without a finishing bridge. Use slow, supervised practice, early taps and immediate release; check division-specific rules before live use.

Instructional sources: [Stephan Kesting and Rob Biernacki — three leg-lock control points](https://www.grapplearts.com/three-critical-control-points-leglock/); [Richie Martinez — Carni shoulder lock from Z guard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iClQ2Np-n30).

flashcards.question: Kneebar after Carni: which new controls must you establish before attacking knee extension?
flashcards.answer: The opponent's thigh and ankle. Confirm control of the opponent's thigh and ankle before considering a knee-extension attack.

Only the head beneath your high leg
trap: Collar grip and the free elbow

flashcards.answer: Moving freely away from the isolated leg. Use the legs to keep the opponent's hip from moving freely away.

Staying aligned with the knee

flashcards.question: Kneebar attack: how should the target knee meet your hips?
flashcards.answer: At the hip fulcrum in a straight, untwisted line. Place the knee at the hip fulcrum with the leg in a straight, non-twisted line.
flashcards.answer_line: Untwisted knee at your hip fulcrum

plausible: Outside hips, toes turned sideways
Folded over shin in the knee crease

flashcards.question: Kneebar attack: what should the ankle grip preserve?
flashcards.answer: A close lower leg without turning the foot. Hold the lower leg close without turning the foot into a rotational lock.
flashcards.answer_line: Close lower leg without foot turning

plausible: Heel twist against a fixed knee
Loose ankle past both forearms

flashcards.question: Kneebar practice: what should a stable capture drill leave out?
flashcards.answer: Bridging into the knee's extension limit. Practice the stable capture without bridging into the knee's end range.
flashcards.answer_line: Bridging to the knee range limit

plausible: Holding ankle close to your body
Placing knee at the hip fulcrum

flashcards.question: Kneebar attack: when should release begin after the partner taps?
flashcards.answer: Immediately, before more extension or either partner turns. Open ankle and thigh control promptly so the leg can move as a whole. Retaining either end while the bodies turn can still load the knee.
flashcards.answer_line: At once, before more load or turning

plausible: After a second confirming bridge
Once they twist their ankle free
trap: Only once thigh control opens itself

flashcards.question: Kneebar attack: where along the hip-to-foot lever does the target joint lie?
flashcards.answer: In the middle, between the two ends. Kesting contrasts a kneebar, which targets the middle joint, with locks at the end of the leg lever. Thigh/hip control, knee alignment at the fulcrum and ankle containment still need to be established separately from Carni.
flashcards.answer_line: In the middle, between both ends

plausible: Beyond the ankle at the far end
Inside the pelvis at the near end
trap: Outside the lever beside the foot

flashcards.question: Kneebar after Carni: why does the original high-leg clamp not supply the kneebar?
flashcards.answer: It clamps a shoulder, not a knee aligned over your hips. Carni is a shoulder-lock configuration. A kneebar needs a separately captured leg and a new hip-to-knee alignment; neither the Carni leg clamp nor its name supplies that alignment.
flashcards.answer_line: It clamps shoulder, not knee at hips

plausible: Its foot position captures the ankle
Its wrist grip also fixes the knee
trap: Any high guard is a knee fulcrum

flashcards.question: Kneebar practice: which lower-limb surfaces sandwich the opponent's hip in Kesting's example?
flashcards.answer: One foot and the opposite calf. The written example contains the hips between a foot and the opposite calf, places the attacking hips at the knee and hugs the foot with the arms. Rehearse capture and full release without a finishing bridge.
flashcards.answer_line: One foot and the opposite calf

plausible: Both insteps stacked on one hip
Two knees above the free-leg thigh
trap: One heel at ankle, other leg free

flashcards.question: Kneebar practice: why should a held ankle not turn while the thigh remains restrained?
flashcards.answer: The knee can receive rotation between the fixed ends. Keep the captured leg untwisted. A held ankle and restrained thigh can transfer a turn into the intervening knee; open both controls before either partner changes direction.
flashcards.answer_line: Knee takes turn between fixed ends

plausible: Ankle turn removes the hip fulcrum
Straight knees cannot take rotation

flashcards.question: Kneebar defense: which arrangement warns of an extension threat?
flashcards.answer: Your knee at their hip fulcrum with your ankle held. A knee trapped at the attacker's hips with the ankle held indicates the extension threat.
flashcards.answer_line: Knee at hip fulcrum, ankle held

plausible: Bent knee with no ankle grip
Shin in knee fold with heel held
trap: Hand only on the outer calf

flashcards.question: Kneebar defense: which grip fixes the far end of your leg beyond the target joint?
flashcards.answer: A secure grip on your ankle and lower leg. Hand fight and keep the lower leg free before the attacker completes the capture.

plausible: A hand pressing above your kneecap
Their calf wrapping behind your hip
trap: One knee squeezing your upper thigh

flashcards.question: Kneebar defense: when should you recover the knee away from the fulcrum?
flashcards.answer: While the leg still has freedom to move. Move the knee away from the fulcrum only while the leg can still move freely.

plausible: Once ankle is fixed, bridge loaded
By turning torso against fixed foot

flashcards.question: Kneebar defense: why is a twisting escape risky when ankle and thigh are both restrained?
flashcards.answer: The knee can take rotation between the fixed contacts. Avoid a twisting escape against a held ankle and trapped thigh.

plausible: Turning frees ankle before knee load
Thigh grip blocks force from foot

flashcards.question: Kneebar defense: why should a secure extension capture be stopped before testing it for pain?
flashcards.answer: Joint load can increase before a useful pain warning. Treat established extension control as the stop point in practice. Do not use pain or remaining range as a test of whether the joint is safe to load farther.
flashcards.answer_line: Load may rise before pain warns

plausible: Pain tests open the thigh restraint
Held ankle prevents full knee range
trap: No pain proves room to bridge again
